original_question: For each d, is the reverse-mathematical strength of the strong-tree version of the Halpern-Lauchli Theorem for d trees strictly stronger than the reverse-mathematical strength of the somewhere dense matrix form for d trees?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Problem (5): "Is the reverse math strength of the strong tree version of Halpern-Lauchli for d trees strictly stronger than the somewhere dense matrix form for d trees?" ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.10227.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact comparison asked in the paper: it identifies the two principles being compared (the strong-tree form and the somewhere-dense-matrix form of Halpern-Lauchli), keeps the parameter d as the number of trees, and asks for a strict reverse-mathematical separation rather than a mere implication. It is very close to the paper's wording. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.10227.pdf))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the base theory should be made explicit: in reverse-mathematical usage, "strictly stronger" should be read as a comparison over RCA_0, even though Problem (5) itself leaves the base theory implicit within the Section 2 reverse-mathematics setting. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.10227.pdf))

The quantifier on d should be sharpened to a fixed finite number of trees (equivalently, a fixed positive integer d), rather than leaving open whether d ranges over arbitrary cardinalities or whether the question is about a uniform schema. Section 1 frames Halpern-Lauchli as a theorem for any finite number of trees. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.10227.pdf))

The ambient setting should be stated: this paper's tree side concerns infinite, finitely branching trees, and nearby context also mentions finitely branching infinite trees with no terminal nodes. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.10227))

The phrase "strictly stronger" should be unpacked as: the strong-tree principle implies the somewhere-dense-matrix principle over RCA_0, but the converse is not provable over RCA_0. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.10227.pdf))

Problem (5) names the two forms but does not restate their definitions; a self-contained version should at least gloss that the strong-tree form asks for monochromatic strong subtrees with a common level structure, while the somewhere-dense-matrix form asks for a monochromatic somewhere dense matrix. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.10227.pdf))

The intended nuance is comparative rather than absolute: the paper explicitly notes that a positive answer here would contrast with results cited in [3] and [4], where these forms are equivalent for strongly inaccessible cardinals over ZFC. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.10227.pdf))
refined_question: For each fixed finite d >= 1, over RCA_0, and for d infinite finitely branching trees with no terminal nodes, is the strong-tree form of the Halpern-Lauchli theorem for d trees strictly stronger than the corresponding somewhere-dense-matrix form for d trees, in the reverse-mathematical sense that the strong-tree principle implies the somewhere-dense-matrix principle but the converse is not provable over RCA_0? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.10227))
justification: This draft clearly targets Section 2, Problem (5), and not a broader neighboring problem: the wording is almost verbatim from that item. I therefore kept the scope narrow and only made explicit the details needed to make the question stand alone: the fixed finite-d quantifier, the ambient tree setting from the paper's title and Section 2 heading, and the meaning of "strictly stronger" as a strict implication over RCA_0. I did not broaden the question to Problem (4) (d versus d+1 trees), Problem (6) (comparison with Milliken's theorem), or the Rado-graph problems. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.10227))
